name: Foreign Employee Work Permit

requirements.blocker_text: The employer must first obtain authorization from the Ministry of Labour, submitting a certified passport copy, identity card copy, and a bank guarantee, before General Security will process an entry visa.
requirements.fix_path: Have the sponsoring employer secure Ministry of Labour authorization.

requirements.blocker_text: Following Ministry of Labour authorization, a General Security visa is required, supported by the ministry authorization, passport/ID copies, a notarized guarantee, and a profession attestation.
A labor permit requires the passport and visa copies, insurance documentation, medical test results, and a notarized work contract.

outcome.duration_length: not confirmed precisely in this build; described as renewable

sources.title: General Directorate of General Security (Lebanon) -- three-stage foreign work authorization process: Ministry of Labour authorization, General Security visa, then labor permit, each with its own document set

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Lebanon). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- direct General Security sourcing, tier 1. The reviewed page is titled around domestic-worker hiring specifically but describes the same three-stage Ministry of Labour / General Security / labor-permit structure reported elsewhere as Lebanon's general foreign-worker authorization process; it was not cross-verified in this build against a separate non-domestic-worker-specific government page, so treat the domestic-worker-specific details (if any diverge for other professions) with some caution even though the route is marked published on the strength of the tier-1 source for the core three-stage process. family_can_join set false (not asserted true without a source) and family_can_work left null -- dependents' rights under this specific permit type were not detailed in the source reviewed; a general family/dependent residency path may exist through a separate application but was not confirmed for this route in this build. work_rights set 'restricted' since Lebanon operates reserved/closed professions for non-Lebanese nationals in numerous fields (law, several other licensed professions), not independently enumerated in full in this build.
